name: A Church Divided: The Reformation and Its Wars
description: From Gutenberg's press and Luther's protest to the Thirty Years' War: how a quarrel over the Church broke Christian Europe into rival camps.

checkpoints.name: Ink and unrest
checkpoints.note: Johannes Gutenberg's printing press made books cheaper, and the Gutenberg Bible was among the first big books printed in Europe. New ideas could now travel faster than the Church could answer them.

checkpoints.name: Luther's protest
checkpoints.note: Martin Luther challenged Church practices in 1517, and the Protestant Reformation spread under the eye of Emperor Charles V. The German Peasants' War broke out, John Calvin began his work, and Henry VIII broke with Rome to create the Church of England. Thomas More was executed in 1535 for refusing to accept it, and the Jesuits were founded in 1540.

checkpoints.name: Rulers, queens and fleets
checkpoints.note: Edward VI, Mary I and Elizabeth I each led England's Church in a different direction. In the Dutch Revolt the Netherlands rose against Spain, and in 1588 the Spanish Armada failed to invade England.

checkpoints.name: Plots and war
checkpoints.note: Guy Fawkes and the Gunpowder Plot failed in 1605, and in 1620 the Mayflower carried the Pilgrims to America. The Thirty Years' War devastated Germany, Gustavus Adolphus led the Swedes, and the Peace of Westphalia ended it in 1648.
